correctness.rationale: For n=bq+r, direct division reduces the gcd to gcd(bq+r, arq+c_r), and every common prime divides t_r. For primes dividing b the common-divisibility condition is a residue-class obstruction gcd(b,r,c_r)>1; for primes coprime to b it is exactly one q-class modulo each prime factor of t_r. CRT yields the stated mean and period. If t_r=0, b|n² and writing n=gm,b=gh,h|g yields gcd(n,an²/b)=n/h; the only success is n=sqrt(b) when b is square. The periodic model plus this spike proves exact onset, and squareclass invariance follows from the explicit congruence c_r difference. Reproduced 1102 parameter cases, 309466 exact original-gcd comparisons, 604026 finite fibre-shift tests, and 91 spike checks using the included verify.py. These finite checks are corroborative; the proof is for all mixed-composite b.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-coefficient quadratic-floor gcd problem has distinct irrational, prime, prime-power, and mixed-composite arithmetic regimes. The mixed-composite regime has genuine interacting denominator-prime obstructions; the result gives an exact rational density at every mixed denominator, a global no-exceptions indicator model, the precise square-denominator onset, and a nontrivial numerator squareclass symmetry. These are complete natural structural invariants and exact distributional data rather than an arbitrary finite slice. It supplies a well-defined boundary alongside the recent irrational quadratic-floor theorem.
